key_insight: LLMs can generate correct finite element code, but inconsistent results and weak self-verification limit trust; separating coder and tester agents shows promise.
engineering_relevance: Automating mechanics code requires independent numerical validation, not just passing an agent’s own checks.
method: Extend FEM-Bench to 17 tasks covering nonlinear mechanics, history dependence, and structural dynamics.
Evaluate 15 models on single-pass implementation and test generation, then compare two execution-enabled agentic harnesses for six models.
Analyze 249 failed agentic trajectories and explore separate coder and tester agents.
evidence_signal: The exploratory coder–tester configuration achieved 97.6% probability of at least one success in three attempts and 88.8% probability that all three succeed, versus at most 78.8% all-three success across the primary model–harness comparisons.
watch_item: Agentic revision can regress performance, and the exploratory coder–tester gains need broader validation before deployment in engineering workflows.
paper_title: Scientific Coding with Large Language Models: Evidence from Finite Element Analysis
